newsitem.title: USA: Daimler chief-Germany should be more nimble.
newsitem.headline: Daimler chief-Germany should be more nimble.

text.p: The chairman of German industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG, Juergen Schrempp, said on Monday that his country needed to adopt American-style economic practices, but not make wholesale changes to its business traditions.
Speaking at the Economic Club of Detroit, Schrempp said that Germany needed to react more nimbly to changes in the world market place.
"We need to modify the "German model" so that we not only reap the benefits of consensus but also adapt ourselves successfully to a world that has significantly changed," he said.
A copy of Schrempp's speech was made available in Frankfurt in advance of his remarks.
German companies, unlike their counterparts in the U.S., have traditionally worked with unions in making business decisions and have taken on a large role in training their work forces.
But Daimler has been a leader in trying to reduce labour costs, earning it criticism from union leaders in Germany.
"The system of consensus cannot mean a system of standing still," Schrempp said.

The Daimler chairman, who has been attacked in the German press for personally leading a campaign to cut costs, said American-style management, where workers are often laid off during short periods of economic down-turn, went too far.
"I want to repeat that the German system of consensus should under no circumstances be abandoned," he said.
"We cannot simply graft Anglo-American business practices on to European industry. Rather we must harness the best elements of both worlds."
Schrempp said a 40 percent increase in Daimler's share price this year proved that financial markets welcomed his cost-cutting plans.
